advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalize/omit an empty-string `assignee` (and other empty values) in the DC create path so `assignee=""` is not sent bare to `client.create_issue`, matching `_assign`'s bug-751e empty-string handling.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:74: `"assignee": ticket.get("assignee") or ""` — the DC create mapper resolves an absent assignee to the empty string, never omission
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:125: `if isinstance(value, str) and value:` — empty string is falsy, so `assignee=""` is not wrapped and passes through

src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:619 `fields=outbound_mapper.map_local_to_remote(ticket, ...)` — the create mutation's fields come from the mapper that emits the empty-string assignee

_people.py:49-70 documents that `assignee=""` on pycontribs is NOT an unassign: it 'either raises ... or, worse, returns a hit and assigns an ARBITRARY user', and `_assign` normalizes `""`→None before the vendor call — the create path has no such normalization
The commit message claims 'an ABSENT field is never invented' but the DC create path never produces an absent assignee; it produces `""`, which this gate lets through unchanged to the vendor create.
advisory.finding: For an unassigned local ticket the DC create payload carries `assignee=""` (an empty string), not an absent key, so the new wrap gate `isinstance(value, str) and value` skips it and `assignee=""` is passed straight to `client.create_issue(**fields)` — the exact empty-string-assignee hazard that `_assign` normalizes away for the update path (bug 751e), where pycontribs treats `""` as a user SEARCH that can error or assign an arbitrary user rather than as an unassign.
scenarios: Any outbound CREATE for a local ticket with no assignee: `_map_local_to_dc_fields` emits `assignee=""`, which reaches `client.create_issue(assignee="")` and can raise or mis-assign on the DC instance.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop or normalize empty-string assignee before the wrap, e.g. treat `""` as unassigned: pop the key (or set `None`) when `isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip()`, rather than leaving the bare empty string to reach the vendor create.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the intended wire shape for `_dispatch_payload(assignee="")` on the DC create path.
evidence: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_create_field_translation_18a5.py:270-272: `payload.pop("priority", None)` / `payload.pop("assignee", None)` — tests only true absence, not empty string
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:74 shows production emits `""`, a shape no test covers
ABSENCE: no test in the file constructs `_dispatch_payload(assignee="")` to pin what reaches the wire for an unassigned create.
test_absent_priority_and_assignee_are_not_invented pops the keys (`payload.pop("priority", None)`) — it exercises the key-absent path, not the value=="" path
ABSENCE: no test in the file passes an empty-string priority or assignee (`search_files` for `priority=""` and `empty` returned no matches)
Module comment at _issues.py:122 states an ABSENT/empty field must not be turned into an object; ticket 544e establishes an unmappable assignee resolves to `""` — the exact input this branch guards
advisory.finding: The new tests exercise the truly-absent case (`payload.pop("assignee", None)`) and the non-empty and already-object cases, but omit the empty-string assignee case that the DC create mapper actually produces (`ticket.get("assignee") or ""` → `""`), so the untested `assignee=""` path passes through unwrapped without any assertion pinning the intended behavior.
merged_from: The empty-string branch of the new wrapping guard (`isinstance(value, str) and value`) is untested: no test passes `priority=""` or `assignee=""`. The `and value` clause is a deliberate discriminator (per the module comment and ticket 544e, an unmappable assignee resolves to `""` and must stay unassigned rather than become `{"name": ""}`), but the tests only cover non-empty string, already-object, and fully-absent inputs. A regression dropping `and value` — sending `{"name": ""}` to Jira — would pass the entire suite.
scenarios: A regression that changes empty-string handling in the create path would not be caught by these tests.
